note: Hebrew tsarua covers a range of scaly skin conditions (and mould on fabric/walls elsewhere), not specifically Hansen's disease (modern leprosy).

mine: loosen the hair of the woman's head
note: Hebrew para' rosh means to let the hair hang loose or dishevelled (a sign of shame or mourning), not necessarily removing a covering.

kjv: gone aside to uncleanness [with another] instead of thy husband
mine: gone astray into uncleanness while under your husband's authority
note: Hebrew tachat ishek means "under your husband", i.e. while married to him; the KJV's "instead of" plus supplied "[with another]" shifts the sense. Same in 5:20, 5:29.

Hebrew yarekh nofelet is literally "a falling thigh", perhaps a euphemism for miscarriage, prolapse or sterility (cf. 5:28 "shall conceive"); "rot" is an interpretation, as is "waste away". Also 5:22, 5:27.
